ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, authorised signatories, and ultimate beneficial owners against: (i) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List implementing UN Security Council resolutions; (ii) Spain's national designation lists administered by the Secretaría de Estado de Economía y Apoyo a la Empresa and Banco de España; (iii) national and EU politically exposed persons (PEP) databases; (iv) the OFAC SDN List as a best-practice banking overlay for USD-clearance and cross-border operations; (v) domestic regulatory warnings and insolvency/disciplinary registries. Screening must be carried out prior to incorporation, on any change of control, and periodically thereafter. Results and risk assessments must be documented and retained for a minimum of ten years in accordance with Ley 10/2010, the LOPDGDD (Organic Law 3/2018), and applicable GDPR principles.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) — electronic application through the Colegio de Registradores de España portal at https://www.registradores.org and https://www.rmc.es
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered name of an SL must be expressed in Spanish or in another European Union language using Latin script; non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet. The statutory suffix 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada' or the abbreviation 'S.L.' must appear exactly as prescribed and cannot be replaced by a foreign-language equivalent. The name must be lawful, not contrary to public order, not misleading as to the company's purpose, and sufficiently distinguishable from names already registered in the Registro Mercantil Central. Names consisting solely of a surname, geographic indication, or official institutional reference are subject to stricter scrutiny.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Colegio (when implying a professional or regulatory college)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registro Mercantil Central issues a positive certificate (refusing the requested negative name certificate), the applicant must: (Step 1) obtain the RMC's written statement of grounds for refusal; (Step 2) file a reconsideration request ('recurso potestativo de reposición') with the RMC within one month of notification, and the RMC must resolve within one month; (Step 3) if refused, file an administrative appeal ('recurso de alzada') with the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (DGSJFP) of the Ministry of Justice within one month of the RMC decision; (Step 4) if still refused, commence 'recurso contencioso-administrativo' before the competent Juzgado de lo Contencioso-Administrativo within two months of the DGSJFP decision. Where refusal rests solely on a prohibited or sensitive token, the applicant may apply to the competent ministry for prior authorisation and then resubmit the same name. All procedural deadlines must be monitored electronically, and the applicant may, in parallel, request a fresh name reservation under a different denomination; the original 90-day reservation may be extended once for an additional 90 days if timely renewal is sought before expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual or serviced office is permissible for an SL engaged in e-commerce sales and contract-manufactured goods, provided that: (i) the virtual office is a genuine physical address in Spain accepted by the Registro Mercantil and AEAT for service of process; (ii) administrative management and books and records are accessible at that address or at a separate documented location; and (iii) the company maintains sufficient substance, such as a bank account, management accounts, and administrative staff. However, where the SL itself carries out double-shot PBT plastic injection manufacturing, a virtual office alone is not sufficient; a physical industrial premise within Spanish territory must be registered and operated in compliance with municipal licensing, health and safety, environmental, and Seguridad Social obligations. A non-compliant virtual office used as the sole seat could trigger AEAT reclassification, loss of Spanish corporate tax residence, or denial of incorporation inscription in the Registro Mercantil.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-high: 35% estimated probability of an unannounced physical inspection by AEAT or social/labor authorities within the first 24 months of operation, increasing to approximately 50% if in-house injection-moulding machinery and imported PBT resin are used. The assessment assumes a low-risk AML profile, no statutory operating license requirement, and the absence of prior regulatory infringement.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Royal Decree 815/2013 for wastewater treatment; VOC emissions below 50 mg/m³; proper hazardous waste handling per EU directives

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from local fire department, structural load inspections, and workplace health and safety clearance from the Ministry of Labour

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); Sede Electrónica: https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es; official portal: https://www.agenciatributaria.es; export and customs enforcement are exercised by the Departamento de Aduanas e Impuestos Especiales of AEAT.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a resident Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) the statutory tax ID is the NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal; formerly the CIF). On incorporation the notary applies by telematics (Form 036) to AEAT for a provisional NIF simultaneously with notarising the public deed; upon inscription in the Registro Mercantil AEAT issues the definitive NIF. The SL then files Form 036 (declaración censal) to join the Censo de Empresarios, declares the applicable VAT regime, and obtains an EORI number (Spain format: ES + NIF) for customs purposes when export activity is planned. A foreign entity without a Spanish establishment that nevertheless engages in taxable Spanish activities (warehousing, fulfilment, direct distance sales, branch) must appoint a resident tax representative, file Form 030/036, and obtain a non-resident NIF (type 'N'), attaching an apostilled or legalised certificate of incorporation with Spanish sworn translation, a notarised power of attorney, and identity documents; requests are processed centrally by AEAT and typically resolved within 1–3 weeks.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain has no check-the-box election; every SL is a resident corporate taxpayer taxed on worldwide income under Ley 27/2014 (Impuesto sobre Sociedades). Statutory elections and special regimes include: (i) consolidated tax group (Arts. 62–73 Ley 27/2014), applied upon unanimous decision where the dominant entity holds at least 75% (or 50% if listed) of the dependent entities and all are Spanish residents; (ii) ETVE holding regime (Arts. 21 and 107 Ley 27/2014) elected on the tax return for exempting foreign dividends and capital gains; (iii) patent box regime (Art. 23 Ley 27/2014) granting a 60% exemption on qualifying IP income; (iv) hybrid mismatch matching rules (introduced by Law 10/2018 and RDL 9/2021) which override classifications and deny deductions automatically without an elective opt-out; (v) accelerated depreciation and free amortisation options for environmentally friendly assets, with all options exercised directly in the annual IS return rather than through a separate entity-classification filing.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), acting as Spain's central bank and the National Competent Authority for credit institutions and payment service supervision under the Single Supervisory Mechanism and PSD2. Foreign trade and foreign direct investment statistical and declaration oversight is jointly administered with the Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones (DGCOMIN) of the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business. There is no separate foreign exchange control office: currency policy and euro convertibility rest with the European Central Bank and the free-movement-of-capital provisions of TFEU Articles 63–66.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility applies to both current-account and capital-account operations. Spain imposes no exchange-control licensing, no prior central-bank approval, and no repatriation quotas for the euro area; the euro (EUR) is the functional treasury currency of the Spanish SL. Capital contributions from non-resident shareholders, dividend remittances, and trade payments to non-EU suppliers may be executed freely in EUR or foreign currency through resident bank accounts, subject only to statistical declaration to Banco de España (monthly C1 reporting for transactions above EUR 50,000 per operation). Profit remittance incurs no convertibility hurdle: only Spanish non-resident income tax at 19% applies to dividends paid to non-resident shareholders, with 0% available under qualifying EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive treatment and treaty-reduced rates for third-country shareholders (Spain–China 10%; Spain–US 10%–15%; Spain–Mexico 15%) on submission of the relevant tax-residence certificate.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender obligation exists in Spain. Export receipts, such as USD collections for custom keyboard keycaps from Shopify/Stripe, may be retained in the original currency in multicurrency accounts, sold forward, or converted to EUR at the SL's sole discretion; there is no mandatory conversion ratio and no statutory repatriation deadline. The only compliance duties are: (a) statistical reporting of each individual cross-border collection or payment above EUR 50,000 to Banco de España under the monthly C1 survey, classified under the merchandise-export heading for collections and merchandise-import heading for supplier payments; and (b) annual Modelo 720 declaration if the SL maintains accounts with non-Spanish financial institutions with aggregate balances above EUR 50,000 per asset category (accounts held at Spanish resident banks in foreign currency do not trigger Modelo 720).

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational EUR current account (Cuenta Corriente) with multicurrency sweep capability for USD/GBP/CNH collections from Shopify and Stripe
Capital deposit / escrow account (cuenta de depósito de capital) for notarial certification of the inbound capital injection, plus an operational EUR account
Operational current account with a dedicated foreign trade settlement desk and SWIFT/Letter-of-Credit execution capability
Operational EUR account with international services and SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst) for intraday float management
Euro-denominated operational account with cross-border liquidity aggregation tools for corporate treasury structuring

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility with strict legal constraints. Only European Economic Area credit institutions or licensed Payment Institutions (EMIs) passporting into Spain under PSD2 — for example Adyen, Wise, CurrencyCloud — may legally hold the SL's float and execute SEPA/SWIFT payments with Spanish IBANs. Non-EU or offshore EMIs (post-Brexit UK, US, or LATAM fintechs) cannot open a Spanish IBAN or receive the statutory capital contribution without a Spanish-licensed agent bank or a Spanish subsidiary authorised by Banco de España; reliance on such an offshore EMI as sole treasury intermediary would invalidate the notarial deposit certificate and break the Banco de España C1 reporting chain. Stripe Payments Europe Ltd (Central Bank of Ireland) and Shopify Payments (powered by Stripe) are permissible as merchant-acquiring rails for card collection, but their settlement payouts must ultimately be swept to a resident tier-1 Spanish bank account; the recommended architecture is therefore: tier-1 bank circuit for capital, FX, and import payments, with a secondary PSP-only circuit for Stripe/Shopify collection with zero treasury float retention.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Fully remote corporate onboarding is not available to a Spanish SL with 100% non-resident ownership. Under Ley 10/2010 (AML), Royal Decree 304/2014 implementing regulations, and Banco de España supervisory criteria, tier-1 banks require at least one physical in-branch KYC interview in Spain, conducted either by (a) a managing director appearing in person with original passport and NIE (Número de Identificación de Extranjero) certificate, or (b) a Spanish-resident administrator or attorney-in-fact appearing with a notarized and apostilled corporate power of attorney executed by all non-resident signatories. Mandatory documentation additionally comprises the original escritura de constitución, the company NIF tax identification, Spanish registered-office proof (recent municipal padrón or lease contract), and a beneficial-ownership declaration under Ley 10/2010. Video-call identification may only be used as a supplementary step for the co-signatory and cannot replace the in-person interview of the corporate legal representative for this entity type.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident director or sole shareholder without a Spanish NIE and without EU residence status
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled passport of each director and shareholder; NIE certificate issued by the Spanish police (Oficina de Extranjería); proof of the SL's Spanish registered office; and a notarized power of attorney appointing a resident representative to attend the physical KYC interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Multi-tier or opaque beneficial-ownership chain, such as a Latin American holding company above the SL
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate organigram of the full shareholder chain; certificate of good standing issued within 90 days; ultimate-beneficial-owner declaration under Ley 10/2010 filed with the Registro Estatal de Titularidades Reales; audited financial statements or a bank reference letter for each intermediate corporate shareholder.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency, low-unit-value e-commerce collections from foreign cardholders via Shopify Payments and Stripe without conventional paper invoices
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed platform service agreements with Shopify and Stripe; monthly PSP settlement statements; transaction-level export order log; customs export declarations (CN23/CN22 or EU exit summary declarations); and the ISIC 3240 product catalogue evidencing low-risk novelty mechanical keyboard keycaps.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection arriving by wire transfer before or after the notarial deed date of the capital increase
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the escritura pública of the capital increase or constitution deed; bank-issued certificate of deposit (certificado de depósito) matching the escrow account; Form D-1A foreign-direct-investment declaration filed electronically with DGCOMIN within 30 days of the deed; and source-of-funds evidence (bank statements and prior distribution resolutions) of the investing shareholder.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound trade payments to Chinese or US polymer-resin suppliers and injection-mould vendors without a visible supply-chain rationale
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed purchase orders with Incoterms; vendor commercial invoices; bill-of-lading or airway-bill evidence; certificate of origin; and matching inventory records for PBT resin and keycap tooling. The SWIFT instruction must carry the statistical purpose indicator for merchandise imports so that the transaction is coherent in the Banco de España monthly reporting.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer protocol: non-resident shareholders transmit the subscription funds via SEPA Credit Transfer (EU/EEA shareholders) or SWIFT MT103 (third-country shareholders, including China, US, and LATAM) to the SL's designated Spanish escrow account at CaixaBank or another tier-1 institution. SWIFT field 70 (Remittance Information) must state: 'Aportación de capital social – [SL legal name] – NIF [code] – escritura fecha DD-MM-YYYY', and the initiating bank must disclose the statistical purpose category to the receiving bank as 'capital contribution / direct investment by non-resident investor'. No prior FDI approval is required for this non-sensitive ISIC 3240 activity under the Spanish FDI screening rules (Law 8/2020); the verification chain is: bank issues the certificado de depósito (deposit certificate) confirming availability of funds; the notary executes the escritura pública; the notary or the SL files Form D-1A with DGCOMIN within 30 days; transactions above EUR 1,000,000 or originating from tax-haven jurisdictions remain declarable and may be subject to post-clearance review. Cash deposits, cheque deposits, and cryptocurrency rails are not legally acceptable for the capital subscription.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements run through three complementary rails: (1) SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) and SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst) for EU suppliers and intraday float liquidity, executed free of charge within the eurozone with maximum ten-second settlement; (2) SWIFT MT103 for non-SEPA vendors — Chinese PBT resin factories, US packaging and tooling suppliers — with the statistical purpose indicator for merchandise imports and Incoterms reference recorded on the bank's payment instruction sheet; and (3) irrevocable documentary Letter of Credit transmitted by SWIFT MT700 for high-value capital equipment, specifically injection-moulding machinery, payable at sight or by 60-day usance tenor through the SL's tier-1 trade desk. For the standard keycap production cycle, the economically efficient rail is MT103 telegraphic transfer with a 30% advance and 70% against shipping documents; the LC route is reserved for tooling purchases exceeding EUR 50,000. All outbound payments must be matched against the supplier proforma invoice and the Spanish customs import declaration (DUA) and retained for the Banco de España C1 monthly statistical reconciliation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Forward Contract (plain vanilla, deliverable) — EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, and EUR/CNH; tenors up to 12 months under the bank's standard master forward confirmation without ISDA for notional amounts at or below EUR 1,000,000.

Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) — EUR/CNY referenced to the offshore CNH fixing, used exclusively to hedge CNY-denominated PBT resin supplier payables because onshore CNY is not freely deliverable outside mainland China.
Cross-Currency Swap (FX Swap / CCS) — EUR/USD and EUR/CNH structures aligning USD revenue receipts from Shopify/Stripe with scheduled vendor disbursement currency exposure.
Zero-Cost FX Collar (option tunnel) — EUR/USD range-forward protecting the budget conversion band without upfront premium, subject to board-approved treasury hedging policy.

Multicurrency account natural hedging — maintaining USD/CNH operational balances in the Santander or BBVA multicurrency sweep accounts as a non-derivative buffer against intra-month settlement timing mismatches between e-commerce receivables and import payables.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts Deposit (Depósito de Cuentas Anuales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month after shareholder approval and no later than 7 months after fiscal-year end (calendar-year company: by 31 July)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry closure (cierre registral) suspending all other filings; fine EUR 1,200–EUR 60,000; denial of good-standing certificates; unresolved closure for 3 consecutive years may lead to administrative dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 days following the 6-month post-close period (calendar-year company: by 25 July)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment surcharge of 5% plus daily interest; flat 20% penalty on unpaid tax; possible asset seizure by AEAT; no commercial-registry strike-off.
Late-filing penalty EUR 300–EUR 20,000 plus 20% surcharge and late-payment interest; no commercial-registry strike-off.
Informational-return penalties from EUR 150 per data item (minimum EUR 300) plus late-payment interest; no commercial-registry strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audit for an SL if, for two consecutive fiscal years, at least two of the three conditions are exceeded: total assets > EUR 3,300,000; annual operating turnover > EUR 6,600,000; average staff > 50 employees. Also mandatory for groups subject to consolidated supervision or sectoral laws.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish PGC (Plan General de Contabilidad) and simplified PGC-PYME for SMEs, which are local GAAP harmonised with EU Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS-EU is used for consolidated accounts of groups.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SL must maintain an internal UBO ledger within the Libro Registro de Socios and update it within 15 days after any share transfer or beneficial-ownership change. There is no standalone annual UBO re-filing unless the company is in an AML-regulated sector; however, the annual accounts memory must disclose every direct or indirect holding exceeding 10% and directors' share-related interests.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members / Shareholders (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Directors (Libro Registro de Administradores)
Register of Contracts with Related Directors (Libro de Contratos con Administradores)
Inventory and Annual Accounts Ledger (Libros de Inventario y Cuentas Anuales)

stage_6.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) filed via AEAT electronic headquarters (Sede Electrónica de la Agencia Tributaria); generally mandatory for legal persons with NIF; XML upload and pre-populated form service; must use Spanish tax representative for non-EU resident payers.
stage_6.reporting_frequency: Annual; plus advance/instalment payments through the separate Modelo 202 in April, October and December.
stage_6.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 25 calendar days following the six-month anniversary of the close of the tax period; for a 31 December year-end this means 1–25 July of the following year; if close 31 March, 1–25 October.
